concepts.title: Credit and Micro Finance in Rural Areas
concepts.definition: Rural development requires an adequate credit system because farmers need money for inputs before harvest; sources range from moneylenders and traders in the informal sector to banks and cooperatives in the formal sector, and self help groups with bank linkage provide micro credit to the rural poor, especially women.
concepts.key_idea: Self help groups pool small savings, lend among members and then borrow from banks, giving the poor credit without collateral.

concepts.title: Agricultural Market System and Diversification
concepts.definition: The agricultural market system requires regulated markets, minimum support price, buffer stocks and public distribution system to protect farmers and consumers, while agricultural diversification into allied activities of livestock, fisheries, horticulture and organic farming raises rural incomes and sustainability.
concepts.key_idea: Diversification spreads risk beyond crop failures and adds value through allied activities like dairy, poultry and fish production.

solution_steps.explain: Recall MSP, buffer stock or PDS in the case.

Note the income or sustainability gain.

concepts.title: Organic Farming, Sustainable Development and Rural Employment
concepts.definition: Organic farming uses organic manure and biopesticides instead of chemical inputs, offering sustainable incomes, healthier food and export prospects though with lower yields initially, while rural employment programmes like MGNREGA provide wage employment and food security to the rural poor.
concepts.key_idea: Organic farming promotes sustainable development by protecting soil fertility and avoiding chemical pollution.
